name: Privacy manifests (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy)
plain: A file in each app and listed SDK that states what data it collects and why, checked by Apple at upload.
meaning: Apple turned self-declared privacy into machine-readable files. Xcode merges them into a privacy report, and tracking domains get blocked for ATT-denied users.

android.note: No manifest file. Play uses the Data safety form and the SDK Index instead.

ios.store_policy: Required in new submissions that use listed SDKs or required reason APIs since 1 May 2024; signed SDK requirement for listed third party SDKs
ios.note: Upload warnings started March 2024; rejection for missing reasons started 1 May 2024. Domains in NSPrivacyTrackingDomains are blocked when ATT is denied.

limits.headline: Can list what the app and its add on tools collect, in a file Apple checks
limits.user_action: Nothing. It is checked when the developer uploads the app, and shown in a privacy report
can: Show what data each tool says it collects and why
Block tracking sites for people who said no to tracking
Flag missing reasons so Apple can reject the upload
cannot: Prove the file is complete without Apple's checks
Apply on Android; Google uses the Data safety form and SDK Index
Skip warnings: rejection for missing reasons began 1 May 2024
limits.differs: Only iPhone (iOS 17 and later) has these files. Android has no such file.

story.what_it_is: A file inside each iOS app that states what data it collects and why, checked by Apple.

marketing.name: Privacy manifest files
marketing.pitch: Apps and SDKs describe the data they collect and the reasons they use certain APIs.

story.for_you: You never read it, but it helps. Xcode can merge the files into a privacy report, and tracking domains can be blocked for people who said no to tracking.
story.for_makers: It turns promises into a file Apple can check at upload. Makers must keep a manifest for the app and each popular SDK, and update it whenever an SDK changes what it collects.

use_cases.example: An ad SDK ships a manifest that lists its tracking domains, so iOS can block them if the user said no.
A game studio adds manifests for four SDKs before upload, or App Store Connect rejects the build.
An analytics tool states that it collects device IDs for analytics only, not ads.
A social app generates a privacy report to compare with its nutrition label.
Researchers read manifests to find SDKs that quietly collect more than the app says.
A developer explains in the manifest that a file timestamp API is only used to show file dates.

story.android_note: Android has no matching file. Google uses the Data safety form and the SDK Index.
story.ios_note: Required for new apps and listed SDKs from spring 2024.

technical_bounds: Apps with unlisted reasons get rejected

history.change: App Store Connect begins emailing warnings
Required reason API declarations enforced from 1 May 2024
